messages.subject: R maximum integer and V-dem model application
parts:
Hello,

I am dealing with the V-dem model (my second post on this topic) and the code is the following:

data {
  int<lower=2> K; // categories
  int<lower=0> J; // raters
  int<lower=0> N; // N country-years
  int<lower=0> C; // countries
  int<lower=-3,upper=K> wdata[N,J]; // data
  int<lower=1,upper=C> cdata[J]; // j country indices
  real gsigmasq; // rater-level gamma variance around country-level gammas
  real gsigmasqc; // country-level gamma variance around world gammasse
  // vector [N] mc;
}
parameters {
  real Z;
  // instead of vector[N] Z;
  ordered[K-1] gamma[J];
  vector[K-1] gamma_mu; // world-level cutpoints
  matrix[C,(K-1)] gamma_c; // country-level cuts, rows are countries
  real<lower=0> beta[J]; // reliability score
}
model{
  vector[K] p;
  real left;
  real right;
  Z ~ normal(0,1); // vague prior
  // Z[i] ~ normal(mc[i],1);
  gamma_mu ~ uniform(-2,2);
  for (c in 1:C) {
    gamma_c[c] ~ normal(gamma_mu,gsigmasqc); // row-access of gamma_c
  }
  for (j in 1:J) {
    gamma[j] ~ normal(gamma_c[cdata[j]],gsigmasq); // note row-access
    beta[j] ~ normal(1,1)T[0,]; // truncated so that > 0
    for (i in 1:N) if (wdata[i,j] != -1) {
        left <- 0;
        for (k in 1:(K-1)) {
          right <- left;
          left <- Phi_approx(gamma[j,k]-Z*beta[j]); // fast approximation to Phi
          p[k] <- left - right;
        }
        p[K] <- 1.0 - left;
        wdata[i,j] ~ categorical(p);
      }
    }
  }

The problem is that when I run this, I get the error message: int variable contained non-int values; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=wdata; base type=int

I have done some research and came across this old post: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/-Wx_HVe5R-M/TIc1EgLVBpcJ. I understand this issue has to do with the maximum integer R can handle. I have set wdata (above in yellow) as real and tried to use the log probability function (increment_log_prob, section 26.3 of Stan manual), but the same error appears.

Any suggestions?

Also:

constrain the variable in its declaration with <lower=-2, upper=2>.

Andrew would very much appreciate a script that gripes
at people who use bounded uniform distributions when not
physically necessary for a parameter.
